1.label: CATALOGUED
1.definition: Verified basic metadata and an authoritative reference. Environmental analysis is not implied; no similarity score is permitted.

2.label: PARTIALLY CHARACTERIZED
2.definition: A documented dataset is associated and a complete measurement window exists, but the data do not support a complete, compatible comparison.

3.label: ANALYTICALLY COMPARABLE
3.definition: Every applicable criterion is DIRECT or PROXY, at least three are DIRECT, with provenance and accepted compatibility.

4.label: REPRODUCIBLE
4.definition: Versioned fingerprint, recorded scripts and a passing offline regeneration of every DIRECT value.

readiness_model.rule:
ASTERRO data-readiness model v3 (Phase IV). Machine-readable, computed from explicit checks.

Four levels (cumulative: a record is at the highest level whose checks AND all lower levels' checks pass):
  1  CATALOGUED               verified basic metadata: source-backed name, valid coordinates, place in the
                              hierarchy. Says nothing about analysis; no similarity score is ever permitted.
  2  PARTIALLY CHARACTERIZED  in addition, a documented, retrievable dataset is associated and a complete,
                              checksummed measurement window was computed from it; the data do not yet
                              support a complete, compatible comparison.
  3  ANALYTICALLY COMPARABLE  a fingerprint in which every applicable criterion is DIRECT or PROXY (none
                              MISSING), with at least three DIRECT criteria, finite values, valid units,
                              provenance for every DIRECT value and an accepted compatibility verdict.
  4  REPRODUCIBLE             in addition: versioned fingerprint with a content hash, every producing script
                              recorded by checksum, and an OFFLINE regeneration of every DIRECT value from the
                              retained inputs that matched at build time.
A record that fails a level-1 check is invalid. Readiness says nothing about scientific validity, confidence,
habitability or mission safety; those are reported separately.
Model history: 2.0.0 used levels 0-4 (0 catalogue, 1 terrain, 2 +environmental measurement); 3.0.0 adopts the
four-level scale, merges the former L1/L2 into level 2, and keeps every L3/L4 check unchanged.

criterion_statuses.DIRECT: Measured with the same or a documented compatible definition as the Earth criterion.
criterion_statuses.PROXY: Stand-in defined by rule; explicitly labelled; identical for every planetary target.
criterion_statuses.N/A: No physical counterpart at this target (e.g. air temperature on the airless Moon).
criterion_statuses.MISSING: A compatible product was not assembled for this target; never imputed.

slope.earth: GMTED2010 30″, Horn slope on a 926.6 m baseline, cell mean
slope.planet: MOLA 463 m / LOLA 118 m DEM binned to 926.6 m, Horn slope, 55.6 km window mean
slope.why: Identical algorithm, baseline and statistic; different source DEMs.

surface_roughness.earth: SD of 926.6 m elevations in the cell
surface_roughness.planet: SD of 926.6 m-binned elevations in the window
surface_roughness.why: Identical algorithm and statistic; window (55.6 km) ≈ Earth cell N–S size.

lst_diurnal_range.earth: MODIS Aqua split-window LST, ~13:30 minus ~01:30 local time
lst_diurnal_range.planet: Surface brightness temperature T(13–14 h) − T(01–02 h) local (true) solar time
lst_diurnal_range.why: Same local-time definition; different instruments and retrievals (MEDA TIRS, REMS GTS, Diviner bolometric vs MODIS LST).

annual_temperature_range.earth: NASA POWER T2M warmest-month minus coldest-month mean
annual_temperature_range.planet: Rover air temperature: max − min of 12 Ls-bin (30°) diurnal means
annual_temperature_range.why: Both annual ranges of near-surface air temperature; Mars 'months' are 30° Ls bins (~56 sols); rover point vs 55 km cell.

aridity.why: Not a measurement; identical for every Mars and Moon target, so it cannot distinguish targets.

elevation.planet: 'thin atmosphere' rule: highest valid Earth cell
elevation.why: Planetary elevations use unrelated datums; the proxy value is identical for every target.
